column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2, update v917504). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys), SDK 21.4.0 (Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0 + subsdk1 + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/, updates/<version>/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).
# handheld: the Switch 2 handheld renders at most 1080p, a quarter of docked 4K's render target memory (the iPhone's budget)
# HeapDef Product: 6.44 GB of heaps in a 7.04 GB root block (AllocateMemoryBlock at main+0xbeb454)
# MKW's NinVirtualAddressHeap (main+0x681134) reports as its free size what the system reports free (QueryMemoryInfo total - used). Without the limit the host left the alias
# region's mapped pages out of the used memory, so the heap never let blocks go: 2.4 GB mapped by the fourth race instead of ~1.2 GB (kartnative 82138ff). Fewer GB = less swap on a
# 16 GB Mac and less compression on the iPhone
# NVN2: main+0xdd0890 requires API major 231 and minor >= 39, else it creates no device (null singleton at main+0x69c020)
# 0: the game paces itself. Its frame-step page (patches.py) only carries the render scale; a target would make the host hold presents in whole vsyncs, which no stub of this game follows
# the iPhone's render scale default: 0.65 = 1248x702 of the handheld 1920x1080 (the slider's steps are 0.05); the Mac keeps 1.0
# Textures the CPU fills after creating them without an NVN flush (EPD engine, as Tears of the Kingdom): without both keys they stayed GPU textures of zeros, which ASTC
# decodes as the error colour, and the world had a magenta cast
